REPORT CONNECTIONS / ALGORITHM EVALUATION

Measure the links we get wrong.

Compare the current matcher with BM25. Inspect the originals behind every result.

AUTHORED SYNTHETIC CONTROLS

Run the fixed methods on the selected authored examples.

What this measures

A related report describes the same underlying event, even if it repeats a source or contradicts the original allegation. Relatedness does not establish truth, independent corroboration or danger.

There are 16 authored queries and 48 candidate reports across two partitions. Each query has three candidates, including difficult negatives. Both partitions and their labels are visible to the developer: this is a diagnostic control set, not independent or blinded validation. Text and story families are checked for overlap across partitions; broader template similarity remains.

Methods, denominators and limits

Current TF-IDF: the actual workbench matcher, using its cosine threshold of 0.18 and minimum three shared tokens. Corpus weighting includes the query report, as in the workbench.

BM25 challenger: fixed k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75; candidate-only corpus statistics, unique query terms and a minimum three shared tokens. Positive scores are ranked without a tuned threshold. Its score is not on the cosine scale. This compares two complete retrieval policies, including different acceptance rules.

Both methods use the same bounded Unicode tokenizer. They use report text and known-by dates; authored labels, explanations and family names are supplied only to the evaluator after ranking. There is no translation, event-date extraction or learned semantic reranker. Publication and recording dates determine availability; they are not event dates.

First-result success counts a related first result over all queries. Wrong, unresolved and empty first results remain separate. Recall@3 is the mean fraction of known related reports retrieved within the first three results. MRR averages reciprocal rank of the first related result; missing results contribute zero. Unresolved candidates are never counted as confirmed errors or confirmed matches. Future candidates are excluded from both corpus weighting and scoring.

Eight examples per partition do not establish deployment accuracy. No parameters are tuned here, no method is promoted automatically, and no workspace, forecast or alert is changed. All results are calculated locally without API charges.
